subject: Post-demo: narrow-slice latency delta & A/B plan vs CloudForge
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@cloudforge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: narrow-slice latency delta & A/B plan vs CloudForge

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations: 

Summary (what we saw today)
- CloudForge reported noticeably lower p95 on long-context (>2k tokens) assistant responses in your internal test harness vs Redwood-hosted default config (~30–40ms delta on our measurement).
- For short-context conversational flows (~<512 tokens) the delta collapses and throughput (tokens/sec) is comparable.

Hypothesis
1) The primary delta looks like microburst tail behavior under multi-tenant batching in our hosted pool (KV cache eviction/redo) rather than a fundamental model compute difference.
2) CloudForge is currently running a higher token-parallelism config and a different kernel path for attention which gives them an edge on that narrow slice.

Proposed next tests (A/B narrow-slice focus)
- A: Re-run your long-context p95/p99 sample with a Redwood dedicated micro-pool (pinned instance, same sequence length distribution) to remove multi-tenant variance.
- B: Run a Redwood runtime experiment toggling continuous-batch window from 40ms -> 20ms and measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
- C: Capture KV-cache hit-rate traces for both runs (will help validate hypothesis #1).

Action items
- I'll pull the sample traces you dropped in the Drive link and convert to a narrow_slice_results-table.csv (attached).
- Jordan / Marissa: can you own scheduling the dedicated micro-pool run and the runtime toggle experiment? We should aim for initial numbers by EOD 2027-12-16.
- Jamie: If you can share the CloudForge kernel/path config (or a sanitized snippet), that helps our infra team rule out gaps quickly.

Attachments: narrow_slice_results-table.csv, draft ab_test-plan.md

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@cloudforge.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: narrow-slice latency delta & A/B plan vs CloudForge

Thanks Jonas — appreciated the clear summary. A couple of quick clarifications from our side:

- We ran two harnesses today: the ‘profiled long-context’ run and a synthetic microburst. The long-context numbers are stable across repeats; I’ll attach the harness config.
- We can share a sanitized snippet of our kernel selection flags (will send to your security contact if needed).

Agree on the test plan. I’ve tentatively blocked Wed morning for the Redwood dedicated run — put me down as available for a short sync once you have the traces.

Best,
Jamie
Head of Integrations
CloudForge

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@cloudforge.ai>
Date: 2027-12-15T08:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: narrow-slice latency delta & A/B plan vs CloudForge

Looping infra/ops notes here so execution is smooth.

Jonas — I scheduled a dedicated micro-pool for 2027-12-16 09:00 PST (2x A100 equiv nodes, isolated). Marissa and I sketched the AB run steps in the attached ab_test-plan.md; highlights below: 

Test matrix (short)
- Baseline: Redwood hosted default config, sample set A (replicate your long-context distribution).
- Toggle-1: reduce batching window to 20ms (same sample A).
- Toggle-2: pin dedicated micro-pool (no multi-tenant queue).
- Toggle-3: both pin + reduced batching.

Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99, median tokens/sec, KV-cache hit-rate, per-request kernel path tag, CPU/GPU utilization per node.

Please note: the run will produce fairly large trace exports (~120MB zipped); I'll upload to the Drive link and add a short readme for what to look at.

Marissa — can you handle the orchestration and ensure the instrumentation tag is present (we need the kernel path tag to correlate).

Thanks — Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Quick operational checklist and risks: 

Checklist before the 12/16 run
- [x] Upload sample sets to Drive (samples_v1.jsonl) — DONE
- [x] Confirm infra reservations (Jordan) — DONE
- [x] Enable per-request kernel path tagging (Stephanie) — IN PROGRESS
- [x] Add KV-cache tracing and expiry windows (Stephanie) — IN PROGRESS
- [ ] Validate CloudForge sanitized kernel snippet (Jamie) — pending

Risk notes
- If CloudForge cannot share kernel flags we still get value from dedicated vs hosted delta; worst-case we can only hypothesize root cause rather than confirm.
- The KV-tracing will add ~6–8% perf overhead; we will subtract that baseline from the final numbers and annotate all plots.

Deliverables scheduled
- 2027-12-16 12:00 PST: raw traces uploaded to Drive + readme
- 2027-12-16 15:00 PST: initial analysis (p95/p99 table + tokens/sec summary)
- 2027-12-17: internal decision note (recommendations for customer-facing FTR)

Marissa
Senior Performance PM

Will sync after the 15:00 upload — Jon
